plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag from a first non-zero hold, needed to calibrate step size and settling time for later holds.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain is right, y rises from ~0.34 after a few seconds lag toward 0.4-0.5, with end slope still positive if not yet settled and small fluctuations around trend from noise.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain at a second, higher amplitude from a low start and whether level can be driven toward target; needed to estimate steady-state u for 0.6 and discriminate dead-zone vs weak gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain holds, y reverses from decay to rise within a few seconds from ~0.06 toward ~0.15-0.35 over 12 s with positive end slope (not yet settled) plus ~+/-0.02 noise; if y stays flat or keeps falling, gain/dead-zone hypotheses are refuted.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Equilibrium gain and settling time at u=0.6, which directly determines the steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 and the controller integral time; extending the same hold separates approaching equilibrium (decreasing slope) from linear unlimited rise.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with long settling is right, y rises from ~0.30 toward ~0.42-0.50 over 9 s with positive end slope (still not settled, slope maybe 0.015-0.025/s) plus +/-0.02 noise, staying well below 0.55; flat or falling would refute gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: How y behaves at u=0 (drain rate and time constant), needed for controller down-action and to lower level safely before testing target-reaching inputs near 0.7.
experiments.expected_observation: If drain plus ~5 s lag hypothesis is right, y decays from ~0.42 toward <0.10 over 20 s with large initial negative slope (~-0.04 to -0.07/s) decreasing toward ~0 in last 5 s, plus +/-0.02 noise; flat or rising would refute H4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-amplitude gain and steady-state input for target 0.6 (H5/H6): a short 0.8 hold from low level discriminates linear vs convex gain and estimates rise rate near target, needed to set controller feedforward without violating safety.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with higher slope at higher u is right, y rises from ~0.02 toward ~0.25-0.35 over 10 s with positive end slope ~0.02-0.03/s (not settled) plus +/-0.02 noise, staying well below 0.55; flat or falling would refute H1/H5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain and linearity near target 0.6, which directly sets controller feedforward and integral gain; a 0.65 hold from 0.34 approaches the band and separates ~0.6-equilibrium from 0.8-equilibrium hypotheses.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with tau ~15s is right, y rises from ~0.34 toward ~0.46-0.52 over 7 s with positive end slope ~0.015-0.025/s (not settled) plus +/-0.02 noise, staying below 0.55; flat or falling would refute H1/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Equilibrium gain and settling time at u=0.65 near target 0.6, which directly sets feedforward and integral time; extending the same hold separates approaching equilibrium (decreasing slope) from linear unlimited rise without a step transient.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H2/H6 are right, y rises from ~0.48 toward ~0.55-0.58 over 5 s with positive end slope ~0.012-0.02/s (still not settled) plus +/-0.02 noise, reaching lower edge of band but staying below ~0.60; flat or falling would refute positive gain near target.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Equilibrium gain and settling time at u=0.65 near target 0.6, which directly sets controller feedforward and integral time; extending the same hold without a step transient separates approaching equilibrium (decreasing slope) from linear unlimited rise.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with tau ~10-18s is right, y rises from ~0.55 toward ~0.58-0.60 over 4 s with positive end slope ~0.008-0.015/s (slightly down from 0.012 as it approaches ~0.63-0.73 equilibrium) plus +/-0.02 noise, staying below ~0.60; flat or falling would refute H1/H6 near target.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Equilibrium gain and settling time at u=0.65 near target 0.6, which directly sets controller feedforward and integral time; extending the same hold without a step transient separates approaching equilibrium (decreasing slope) from linear unlimited rise.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H2/H6 are right, y rises from ~0.58 toward ~0.60-0.63 over 4 s with positive end slope ~0.008-0.012/s (still not settled, slightly down as it approaches ~0.65-0.75 equilibrium) plus +/-0.02 noise, entering/staying in lower half of band but below ~0.64; flat or falling would refute positive gain near target.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state u needed to hold 0.6 and local gain near the top of the band; dropping 0.65 to 0.5 separates 0.6-equilibrium from 0.75-equilibrium and measures down-action needed for controller feedforward and integral tuning.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H6 are right, y starts ~0.63 and flattens to ~0.60-0.64 over 4 s with end slope ~0 to -0.01/s (down from +0.0107/s at u=0.65) plus +/-0.02 noise, staying in band; continued rise at +0.01/s would refute the 0.6-holds-0.6 estimate.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 after E10 surprise; extending the same 0.5 hold without a new step separates true 0.5-equilibrium near 0.64 (flat continues) from lag transient after 0.65-to-0.5 step (slope turns negative) and from higher equilibrium (rise resumes), which directly sets controller feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If lag-transient plus ~0.5-holds-~0.64 is right, y stays ~0.62-0.66 in band over 4 s with end slope falling from +0.0028 to ~-0.01 to +0.005/s plus +/-0.02 noise, staying below ~0.67; resumed rise at +0.01/s would imply y_inf at 0.5 well above band, clear fall at <-0.01/s would imply y_inf well below 0.64.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 for feedforward; 0.65-to-0.5 flat could be lag transient or true ~0.64 equilibrium, and a small step to 0.45 separates fall-to-band from continued rise.
experiments.expected_observation: If 0.5-holds-~0.63 is right, y starts ~0.61 and stays ~0.58-0.63 in band over 4 s with end slope ~-0.015 to +0.005/s plus +/-0.02 noise; resumed rise at +0.01/s toward 0.65+ would refute it and imply y_inf at 0.5 well above band.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direct dead-time and drain rate at u=0, which separates longer delay (flat/continued response to prior command before fall) from faster outflow (steeper fall) and weaker gain (same fall) and sensor offset (non-zero floor), needed to set integral time and feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If longer-delay is right, y from ~0.39 stays flat or rises slightly to ~0.40-0.50 for first ~8-15 s while prior ~0.5-0.6 commands in transit arrive, then falls toward <0.20 over remaining ~25 s with late slope ~-0.015 to -0.03/s plus +/-0.02 noise; immediate steady fall from t=0 would refute long delay, flat floor near 0.35 would imply sensor offset.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether delay persists on rising edge versus weak gain, which determines if controller needs delay compensation versus higher feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If long ~25 s delay is right, y stays ~0.02-0.08 flat for the full 15 s with slope ~0 +/-0.01 plus +/-0.02 noise, showing no rise to the 0-to-0.5 step because delay has not elapsed; rise within ~2-5 s toward ~0.15-0.30 would refute long delay and favor short-delay/weak-gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether steady gain at u=0.5 is normal versus weak once delay elapses, which sets feedforward for target 0.6 and determines if delay compensation alone suffices.
experiments.expected_observation: If long ~25 s delay is right, y stays ~0.00-0.04 flat with slope ~0 +/-0.01 for first ~10 s (15-25 s total since 0-to-0.5 step at 340) then starts rising toward ~0.08-0.20 in last ~6 s with positive end slope; immediate continued flat with no rise would imply even longer delay or dead-zone, early rise would refute long delay.

ledger.statement: Increasing constant u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); u=0 drains, u=0.6/0.65/0.8 all drive rise from low level, and E13 drains to 0.013 at u=0 consistent with positive gain. E14 flat at 0.5 for 15 s is delay transient, not refutation.

Response starts within ~2 s with no long pure delay and tau ~12-18 s; E13 refutes this for changed machine by holding ~0.32 flat for ~25 s after 0.6-to-0 step before falling, and E14 shows no rise 15 s after 0-to-0.5 step.
There is no large dead-zone up to 0.65; u=0.6, 0.65 and 0.8 clearly drive rise from low level so any dead-zone is <0.6. E14 flat at 0.5 for 15 s is explained by 25 s delay, not dead-zone >0.5.
At u=0, y drains toward equilibrium at or below ~0.02 near zero; E4 fell 0.423 to 0.02 in 20 s, E13 fell ~0.32 to 0.013 with late slope -0.0127/s, E14 holds ~0.003 mean at low level.
Steady-state y versus u is nonlinear with saturation near target; E10-E11 holding ~0.63-0.64 flat for 8 s at u=0.5 contradicts linear extrapolation.
Holding y at target 0.6 required steady u ~0.45-0.52 in discovery; changed-machine steady gain not yet re-measured because E14 15 s at 0.5 has not yet elapsed delay.
Sensor noise std is <0.02 with no large offset; E13 floor 0.013 and E14 floor 0.0 with scatter ~0-0.015 consistent with discovery plus delay transient.

Changed machine has weaker actuator: same constant u gives smaller rise rate and lower steady y than discovery, e.g. u=0.5 would hold well below 0.63. E14 shows zero rise not small fast rise, favoring delay over weak gain.

Changed machine has faster outflow: fall at u=0 is faster than E4 fall 0.423 to 0.02 in 20 s and same u holds lower y than discovery. E13 late slope -0.0127/s similar to E4 -0.0147/s refutes faster outflow.

Changed machine has longer delay/slower response ~25 s: first visible fall after COMMAND LAST CHANGED occurs ~25 s later versus ~2 s in discovery, causing flat then fall and oscillation. E13 flat ~300-325 s then fall, E14 flat 15 s after 0-to-0.5 step confirms on rising edge.
Changed machine has altered sensor: offset >0.03 or noise std clearly >0.02 versus discovery <0.02. E13 floor 0.013 and E14 floor 0.0 with small scatter refute offset/noise change.
